result.overall: The Federal Court set aside the Appeal Division's decision granting leave to appeal, finding legal errors and a lack of transparency in its reasons, and remitted the matter for redetermination.

themes.name: Legal Error on Medical Evidence
themes.summary: The Appeal Division erred in law by misinterpreting the requirement for objective medical evidence relating to the MQP.

themes.name: Transparency and Reasoning
themes.summary: The Appeal Division's reasons lacked transparency and failed to clearly communicate the basis for granting leave.

themes.name: Standard of Review
themes.summary: The Court applied the reasonableness standard to the Appeal Division's decision.

themes.name: Grounds for Leave to Appeal
themes.summary: The statutory grounds and test for granting leave to appeal were central to the decision.

arguments.claim: The Appeal Division incorrectly found an error of law by the General Division regarding the requirement for medical evidence at the MQP.
arguments.authority: Brennan v Attorney General of Canada, 2011 FCA 318
arguments.quote: The Appeal Division was incorrect to conclude that the General Division erred in law on this issue.

arguments.claim: A claimant must provide objective medical evidence to support a finding of disability on or before the MQP.
arguments.quote: a claimant must provide objective medical evidence to support a finding of disability on or before the MQP

arguments.claim: Ms Angell did not have a reasonable chance of success on the merits of the appeal, so leave should have been refused.
arguments.quote: I will not address that issue in these reasons, as it is a question for the Appeal Division.

holdings.statement: The standard of review is reasonableness.
holdings.quote: The standard of review on this application is reasonableness

holdings.statement: The Appeal Division erred in law regarding the requirement for objective medical evidence relating to the MQP.
holdings.quote: The Appeal Division was incorrect to conclude that the General Division erred in law on this issue.

holdings.statement: The Appeal Division's reasons lacked transparency and failed to communicate the basis for granting leave.
holdings.quote: the Appeal Division’s reasons did not sufficiently communicate what it decided and why

holdings.statement: The decision of the Appeal Division granting leave to appeal is set aside and remitted for redetermination by a different member.
holdings.quote: the decision of the Appeal Division granting leave to appeal must be set aside.

rebuttals.point: The Appeal Division found an error of law by the General Division regarding medical evidence.
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court found this was a legal error and not supported by the law.
rebuttals.quote: The Appeal Division was incorrect to conclude that the General Division erred in law on this issue.

rebuttals.point: Ms Angell did not have a reasonable chance of success on the merits.
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court declined to decide this, leaving it for the Appeal Division.
rebuttals.quote: I will not address that issue in these reasons, as it is a question for the Appeal Division.

authorities.authority: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65
authorities.why: Sets out the reasonableness standard and requirements for justification, transparency, and intelligibility.

authorities.authority: Brennan v Attorney General of Canada, 2011 FCA 318
authorities.why: Clarifies the requirement for disability to exist prior to and continuously after the MQP.
authorities.quote: a claimant must demonstrate an entitlement to disability benefits by reason of a severe and prolonged disability that existed prior to the expiry of the MQP and continuously thereafter

authorities.why: Confirms the need for objective medical evidence to support disability at the MQP.
authorities.quote: a claimant must provide objective medical evidence to support a finding of disability on or before the MQP

authorities.why: Cited for the requirement of objective medical evidence.
authorities.quote: see also Warren v Canada (Attorney General), 2008 FCA 377

authorities.why: Cited for standard of review and objective medical evidence requirement.

authorities.authority: Vancouver Airport Authority v PSAC, 2010 FCA 158
authorities.why: Cited for transparency in administrative decision-making.
authorities.quote: transparency “speaks to the ability of observers to scrutinize and understand what an administrative decision maker has decided and why”

authorities.why: Cited for the requirement of transparency in administrative reasons.
authorities.quote: This general approach denies Ms. Boros the opportunity to understand why the process took so long.

left_open.issue: Whether Ms Angell had a reasonable chance of success on the merits under s. 58(2).
left_open.reason: Left for the Appeal Division to decide on redetermination.
left_open.quote: I will not address that issue in these reasons, as it is a question for the Appeal Division.
